Requirements:

- Give each case fresh setup, invoke production code and include a meaningful assertion.

raw_plan_system_prompt:
You are planning regression characterisation tests for existing C# production code.
Work only from observable public behaviour in the pristine source and neutral dependency
context. Do not diagnose, improve, refactor or repair the production code.

Return ONLY one JSON object with suite_name and exactly five cases. Use these identifiers
and categories once each, in this order:
- H1 / happy_path: one representative valid end-to-end flow.
- E1 / empty_or_invalid: the most relevant empty, minimal, null or invalid-input flow.
- B1 / boundary_values: below, at and above one source-supported boundary. Put all three
  stimuli in inputs. If there is no numeric threshold, use the closest three-point
  cardinality or ordering boundary supported by the public contract.
- A1 / alternative_path: a materially different valid branch, mode or input partition.
- D1 / dependency_or_state: a deterministic dependency outcome, repeated invocation,
  duplicate input or state transition, choosing the first applicable option in that order.

Each case must contain case_id, category, source_evidence, input_partition, inputs and
expected_observation. Every input partition must differ. Evidence and expected observations
must describe behaviour visible in the supplied pristine code; do not invent requirements.
Do not include C# test code in this planning response.

cases.source_evidence: Rows with record type "ORDER" create Web orders. Valid SKU/quantity pairs become lines; STD-prefixed SKUs receive unit price 4.99, while PRM-prefixed SKUs with quantity greater than 10 receive 9.99. Orders with lines are added to the repository and returned.
cases.input_partition: Valid Web order containing multiple valid line pairs

cases.source_evidence: Null or whitespace rows, rows with fewer than four fields, empty references, unsupported record types, and orders with no accepted positive-quantity lines are skipped.
cases.input_partition: Batch composed entirely of null, blank, malformed, unsupported, or line-invalid rows

cases.source_evidence: A PRM-prefixed line receives unit price 9.99 only when quantity is greater than 10; valid positive quantities not satisfying that condition retain the initialized price of 0.
cases.input_partition: PRM quantity immediately below, at, and above the greater-than-10 pricing boundary

cases.source_evidence: Record type "M" creates a Marketplace order. A valid positive-quantity SKU with neither PRM nor STD prefix is retained with the initialized unit price of 0.
cases.input_partition: Valid Marketplace order with an unpriced SKU prefix

cases.source_evidence: For an accepted order, ImportBatch calls OrderRepository.Add. The repository stores orders by reference using dictionary assignment, so adding the same reference replaces the existing value without increasing Count.
cases.input_partition: Valid import whose reference already exists in repository state
cases.expected_observation: {"returned_order_count":1,"repository_count":1,"repository_lookup":{"reference":"EXISTING-1","channel":"Web","lines":[{"sku":"STD-NEW","quantity":2,"unit_price":4.99}]},"state_change":"The previously stored Phone order is replaced by the newly imported Web order."}
